question: A laundromat can buy two types of washing machines, a top-loading model and a front-loading model. The top-loading model can wash 50 items per day while the front-loading model can wash 75 items per day. The top-loading model consumes 85 kWh per day while the front-loading model consumes 100 kWh per day. The laundromat must be able to wash at least 5000 items per day and has available 7000 kWh per day. Since the top-loading machine are harder to use, at most 40% of the machines can be top-loading. Further, at least 10 machines should be front-loading. How many of each machine should the laundromat buy to minimize the total number of washing machines?

import pyomo.environ as pyo

DATA = {

    "capacity_front": 75,        # items per day, front-loading
    "energy_top": 85,            # kWh per day, top-loading
    "energy_front": 100,         # kWh per day, front-loading
    "min_items_per_day": 5000,   # must be able to wash at least this many items
    "max_kwh_per_day": 7000,     # available energy per day
    "max_top_fraction": 0.40,    # at most 40% of machines may be top-loading
    "min_front": 10,             # at least this many front-loading machines
}

def build_model(data=None):
    d = data or DATA
    m = pyo.ConcreteModel()

    # --- Sets ---
    m.M = pyo.Set(initialize=["top", "front"])

    # --- Variables ---
    m.x = pyo.Var(m.M, within=pyo.NonNegativeIntegers)

    # --- Objective: minimize total number of machines ---
    m.obj = pyo.Objective(
        expr=m.x["top"] + m.x["front"],
        sense=pyo.minimize,
    )

    # --- Constraint: items washed per day must be at least 5000 ---
    def items_rule(mm):
        return (
            d["capacity_top"] * mm.x["top"]
            + d["capacity_front"] * mm.x["front"]
            >= d["min_items_per_day"]
        )
    m.items_constraint = pyo.Constraint(rule=items_rule)

    # --- Constraint: energy used per day must be at most 7000 kWh ---
    def energy_rule(mm):
        return (
            d["energy_top"] * mm.x["top"]
            + d["energy_front"] * mm.x["front"]
            <= d["max_kwh_per_day"]
        )
    m.energy_constraint = pyo.Constraint(rule=energy_rule)

    # --- Constraint: at most 40% of machines may be top-loading ---
    # x_top <= f * (x_top + x_front)
    # => (1 - f) * x_top - f * x_front <= 0

        f = d["max_top_fraction"]
        return (1 - f) * mm.x["top"] - f * mm.x["front"] <= 0
    m.top_share_constraint = pyo.Constraint(rule=top_share_rule)

    # --- Constraint: at least 10 front-loading machines ---
    def front_min_rule(mm):
        return mm.x["front"] >= d["min_front"]
    m.front_min_constraint = pyo.Constraint(rule=front_min_rule)

    return m

"""
Laundromat machine-purchase MILP

Decision variables
------------------
x_top   : integer number of top-loading washing machines   (>=0 Integer)
x_front : integer number of front-loading washing machines (>=0 Integer)

Objective
---------
minimize  x_top + x_front
  (minimise the TOTAL number of washing machines)

Constraints
-----------
(1) items/day   : 50*x_top + 75*x_front >= 5000
(2) kWh/day     : 85*x_top + 100*x_front <= 7000
(3) 40% top max : x_top <= 0.4*(x_top + x_front)  ->  0.6*x_top - 0.4*x_front <= 0
(4) front >= 10 : x_front >= 10
"""

import pyomo.environ as pyo

DATA = {
    "items_top": 50.0,         # items/day per top-loading machine
    "items_front": 75.0,       # items/day per front-loading machine
    "min_items": 5000.0,       # minimum items/day
    "kwh_top": 85.0,           # kWh/day per top-loading machine
    "kwh_front": 100.0,        # kWh/day per front-loading machine
    "max_kwh": 7000.0,         # maximum kWh/day
    "top_fraction_max": 0.40,  # top-loading <= 40% of machine total
    "min_front": 10,           # >= 10 front-loading machines
}

GOLD_ANSWER = None


def build_model(data=None):
    d = data or DATA

    model = pyo.ConcreteModel(name="laundromat_machines")

    # ---------------------------------------------------- Variables
    model.x_top = pyo.Var(within=pyo.NonNegativeIntegers, bounds=(0, None))
    model.x_front = pyo.Var(within=pyo.NonNegativeIntegers, bounds=(0, None))

    # ---------------------------------------------------- Objective
    def obj_rule(m):
        return m.x_top + m.x_front

    model.obj = pyo.Objective(rule=obj_rule, sense=pyo.minimize)

    # ------------------------------------------ Constraint (1): items/day
    def rule_items(m):
        return (
            d["items_top"] * m.x_top + d["items_front"] * m.x_front
            >= d["min_items"]
        )

    model.items_req = pyo.Constraint(rule=rule_items)

    # ------------------------------------------ Constraint (2): kWh/day
    def rule_kwh(m):
        return (
            d["kwh_top"] * m.x_top + d["kwh_front"] * m.x_front
            <= d["max_kwh"]
        )

    model.kwh_req = pyo.Constraint(rule=rule_kwh)

    # ------------------------------------------ Constraint (3): top <= 40% of total
    # x_top <= f*(x_top + x_front)  ->  (1-f)*x_top - f*x_front <= 0
    def rule_ratio(m):
        f = d["top_fraction_max"]
        return (1.0 - f) * m.x_top - f * m.x_front <= 0.0

    model.top_ratio = pyo.Constraint(rule=rule_ratio)

    # ------------------------------------------ Constraint (4): front >= 10
    def rule_min_front(m):
        return m.x_front >= d["min_front"]

    model.min_front_req = pyo.Constraint(rule=rule_min_front)

    return model
